thesisQuality.note: Strong recent demand/adoption across aerospace, automotive and packaging plus qualified alloy/process know-how, tempered by cyclical shortage and metal effects.

financialOperatingMomentum.note: Revenue +31% YoY, $148M net income, $90M FCF, leverage 1.8x and raised EBITDA/FCF guidance support the upper strong band, below exceptional because metal-price lag materially aided headline EBITDA.

marketValuationOpportunity.note: Approximately $3.46B current market capitalization is modest relative to the revenue base and improving FCF, but leverage/cyclicality and metal-price normalization constrain the valuation case.

catalystScore.note: Raised 2026 EBITDA and FCF guidance plus expectation of reaching 2028 targets two years early provide identifiable near/medium-term operating catalysts.

governancePower.note: Management has raised guidance as execution improved and reports leverage/FCF transparently, but cumulative evidence does not establish exceptional long-duration capital-allocation or incentive alignment.

alignment2036.note: Aerospace, mobility, packaging and recycling tie the company to durable transport/material-efficiency needs; relevance is strong but the company does not own an irreplaceable raw-material layer.

crossDivisionLeverage.note: Aerospace/TID, packaging and automotive provide multiple demand channels that reuse alloy, conversion and recycling capabilities, though end-market cyclicality remains correlated.

bottleneckControl.note: Qualification and manufacturing know-how create switching friction, but competing aluminum processors and alternate materials prevent treating Constellium as controller of a system-critical bottleneck.

scenarioRobustness.note: Diversified aerospace, automotive and packaging exposure plus recycling optionality support several demand paths, while metal, energy and macro sensitivity remain material.

substitutionResilience.note: Qualified alloys and process know-how create moderate replacement barriers, but competing processors and alternative materials remain credible substitutes.

supplyChainResilience.note: Recycling and higher scrap capture reduce primary-metal dependence, but primary aluminum, scrap spreads, energy and regional trade remain meaningful dependencies.

pricingPower.note: Record segment EBITDA and shortage/qualification dynamics indicate some value capture, but favorable scrap spreads and shortages may normalize and metal-price lag distorts headline economics.

risk.note: Moderate risk from cyclical metal-price lag, shortage normalization, scrap/energy exposure, leverage and substitution; improved FCF and leverage keep risk below the weak/high-risk bands.

confidence.note: Recent primary operating evidence and exact identity/tradability lineage are strong, with current independent valuation context; confidence is reduced by issuer concentration and unresolved customer/program economics.

thesis: Constellium combines qualified high-value aluminum conversion with recycling capacity across aerospace, automotive and packaging; improving FCF/leverage and raised guidance strengthen the case, while durable value depends on execution surviving normalization of metal and shortage tailwinds.
keyRisk: Current profitability can overstate structural economics because metal-price lag, scrap spreads and product shortages may normalize while input and end-market cyclicality remain.
nextCatalyst: Delivery against raised 2026 metal-lag-excluded adjusted EBITDA and >$300M free-cash-flow guidance, with continued leverage reduction.

scoreBreakdown.note: earthScore is the evidence-weighted component score candidate; risk and confidence are preserved separately for canonical runtime application rather than double-applying an unverified transform in specialist evidence.
